input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the accessibility
audit in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation, workbench spawn, model
deployment, and pipeline run submission — so that each flow is fully operable by
keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible
focus indicators. This is the code-level deliverable of the keyboard accessibility
conformance strategy; the published conformance documentation that reflects this fixed
state is handled separately by the documentation work stream.

## Scope

- Fix focus loss and focus traps in modals encountered across the four audited flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission).
- Make every control reachable and operable in those flows via keyboard alone,
  resolving each unreachable-control defect enumerated in the audit report.
- Apply a consistent, visible focus indicator pattern across all controls in the four
  audited flows, aligning to the correct indicator styling already present in parts of
  the console so the indicators are uniform.
- Resolve or explicitly disposition every defect item the audit report lists for the
  four flows.
- Incidental documentation touch-ups that fall out of these fixes (e.g., updated
  screenshots or references in existing Dashboard docs) are included here; substantive
  conformance content authoring (VPAT, accessibility statement) is out of this epic.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and any
  flow outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows can be completed end-to-end using only the keyboard,
  verified by a per-flow walkthrough of the audit defect list, with no focus traps and
  no unreachable controls.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is resolved, or
  explicitly dispositioned with a recorded reason where the audit item is deemed not a
  defect.
- Focus indicators are visible and stylistically consistent across all interactive
  controls in the audited flows.
- The Dashboard's existing automated test suites pass with the changes, and regression
  coverage for the fixed focus behavior is added where the repository's test framework
  supports it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no
  focus traps or unreachable controls: covered by the modal focus-trap fixes and
  keyboard-operability remediation in Scope.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows:
  covered by the focus-indicator consistency work in Scope; bundled with HLR-1 because
  it applies to the same four UI surfaces and the same audit defect list, and is not
  separately schedulable from the operability fixes on those surfaces.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates the accessibility conformance documentation — the VPAT and the
product documentation accessibility statement — to reflect the fixed keyboard
accessibility state of the four core Dashboard flows (project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission), and republishes both artifacts
through the Red Hat docs content process after technical review. Two public-sector
customers require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the
published documentation is a first-class deliverable of this strategy alongside the
code fixes.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT so its conformance claims for the four audited flows reflect the
  remediated keyboard-accessibility state (operability, focus traps, focus indicators).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to match the remediated
  state.
- Keep the conformance claims scoped to what the keyboard fixes actually deliver —
  screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require and flows outside the
  four audited ones are out of scope for this strategy and must not be claimed as
  conformant.
- Route both artifacts through the Red Hat docs content process for republication.
- Obtain technical review of the updated content against the implemented keyboard
  accessibility fixes before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the fixed state of the four audited flows, with each
  updated conformance claim traceable to the implemented remediation.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated to reflect the remediated state.
- The updated content is technically reviewed against the implemented keyboard
  accessibility fixes by an engineer familiar with the remediation, with the review
  sign-off recorded, before republication.
- Both artifacts are republished and live at their existing documentation locations.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs
  accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with
  technical review: covered in full by this epic's Scope and Acceptance Criteria.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

**Strategy**: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

**Triage outcome**: Full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only). Although the
strategy is small, it spans two components (Dashboard, Documentation) and two distinct
work streams: frontend code remediation in the Dashboard, and substantive conformance
content authoring (VPAT update, accessibility statement rewrite and republication). The
multiple-work-streams escape condition for below-threshold applies; a docs-only triage
does not apply because the Dashboard requires code changes.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001: Keyboard accessibility remediation (Dashboard)"] --> E002["E002: Conformance docs update and republish (Documentation)"]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by ALL Implementation epics) | The VPAT and accessibility statement must describe the fixed state, so the conformance documentation cannot be finalized until the keyboard accessibility fixes are implemented. This is the only Implementation epic in the strategy, so docs-authoring is blocked by it alone. |

No Investigation epics: the strategy's Open Questions section is empty and the audit
report enumerates the exact defects per flow, so there are no unknowns whose resolution
would change which epics exist or what they do.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | E001 | Four audited flows fully keyboard-operable; core remediation epic. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | E001 (bundled) — focus-indicator consistency applies to the same four UI surfaces and the same audit defect list as HLR-1; the indicator work is not separately schedulable from the operability fixes on those surfaces, so a split would touch every flow twice. | Same component, same team, one remediation pass. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | E002 | VPAT and accessibility statement update, republication, technical review. |

All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted Teams table,
  no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no Non-Functional
  Requirements section. Decomposition proceeded from the HLRs, Affected Components list,
  and problem statement. Team assignments were inferred: the Dashboard team
  (RHOAI Dashboard) is corroborated by the architecture context file
  (`.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`); the
  Documentation owner (RHOAI Documentation) is inferred — no architecture-context file
  exists for the Documentation component to corroborate it.
- **Epic size above the ~2-week guideline (E001)**: E001 remediates four core flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission); by
  typical modal/focus remediation effort this is plausibly ~2 sprints, above the
  2-week guideline. Kept whole because HLR-2's focus-indicator consistency spans all
  four flows as one shared pattern and the audit verification is a single pass — a
  per-flow split would fragment the shared indicator work and audit each flow twice.
  Re-split trigger: if remediation of the first two flows exceeds one sprint (pace
  projecting four flows past 2 sprints), split the remaining flows into per-flow epics
  under the same team, carrying the shared indicator-consistency work in the flow where
  the canonical pattern is established.
- **Possible priority understatement (non-blocking)**: HLR-3 is P2 (consistent with the
  strategy frontmatter priority `Normal` and the docs-authoring priority exception),
  but the problem statement ties the published VPAT to two public-sector customer
  renewals. If those renewals are near-term, the documentation epic is
  business-critical despite its P2 label — planners should confirm the renewal dates.
- **Scope trap avoided**: the strategy's Out of Scope excludes screen-reader semantics
  beyond what the keyboard fixes require; the conformance documentation epic must not
  claim broader conformance than the keyboard fixes deliver, or the VPAT would assert
  scope the implementation does not cover.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing. All work is internal to
the Dashboard and Documentation components, and there are no upstream or third-party
dependencies.
